claim: Night air at 20 C and 40 % RH carries about 6.92 g/m3 of water vapour [A1]
law: Ideal gas law on the saturation pressure (Magnus form); independent of the CAL's IAPWS fit

claim: Overnight uptake of the 4 kg bed (0.54 kg [B5]) stays below its equilibrium capacity at 40 % RH (1.0 kg CaCl2 as a 40.1 wt % solution plus 0.08 kg/kg per unit activity on 3.0 kg of gel)
law: CaCl2 solution water activity (Conde 2004); salt in the pores held as solution above deliquescence

claim: The fan's night air supplies more vapour than the bed takes up (2.77 kg carried [B4] against 0.54 kg adsorbed [B5])
law: Mass balance on the air stream

claim: Drawing 40 m3/h down through the 9.3 mm beds costs about 0.16 Pa [B3], well within a 2 W, 120 mm fan (about 3.3 Pa for the whole box [F3])
law: Ergun equation, 3.5 mm beads, bed voidage 0.40

claim: The sun is absorbed on a black surface over the beds with transmittance-absorptance about 0.70 [C11]. Was 0.74 on the bare beads, which are white (absorptance about 0.3): the v0.7 design would have made 0.03 L per day [C11]; fixed with black perforated absorber plates on the beds
law: Transmittance of 10 mm twin-wall polycarbonate (about 0.78) times absorptance; a 22.7 % open black plate with light through the holes scattered back onto its underside; cannot exceed the plain black plate (0.78 x 0.95)

claim: Day energy balance closes: absorbed 3.46 kWh [C7] covers desorption, loss through the glazing and heat to the condenser
law: First law over the day; the remainder is sensible heat left in the bed at dusk

claim: Desorbing the night's water takes 2.58 MJ/kg, at least the latent heat of water
law: Heat of desorption of a salt solution is at least the latent heat (2.26 MJ/kg at 100 C)

claim: Solar-to-water efficiency of 5.4 % [C7] for a single-stage sorption collector
law: Published outdoor results: about 9 % for a dual-stage zeolite device (LaPotin et al., Joule, 2021); a single stage recovers no latent heat, so it should sit below that; the independent review recalls single-stage devices at a few per cent (unverified)
check: 5.4 % below about 9 %, but high for a single stage; rests on the estimated absorber figures

claim: Vapour crosses the gap and the drip screen to the condenser at about 96 g/h at its peak (C2); the tray floor lets 58 % of the bed area through. Was 60 % for a 50 % perforated sheet under a fine mesh, about 25 % in fact (independent review); fixed with an open floor of bars and a coarser mesh
law: Stefan diffusion through still air over the open share of the tray floor; hot over cold and moist (light) over dry is stably stratified; estimate taken at the noon state of the v0.8 day table

claim: Condensation happens: at noon saturation at the condenser plate (value) is below the bed's vapour pressure (limit)
law: Vapour pressure of the bed (water activity x saturation at bed temperature) against saturation at the plate

claim: Fins shed heat by natural convection at about 4.7 W/(m2 K) [C8], holding the condenser within 15 K of the air
law: Laminar isolated vertical plate, Nu = 0.59 Ra^0.25, gives 5.0 W/(m2 K); but the fins hang under a hot, tilted, downward-facing floor that traps warm air (independent review): 30 % less convection gives about 14 K, and also half the radiation about 16 K
check: PR-005 at risk; condenser temperature to be logged at TRL 4

claim: The finned underside also radiates to the shaded ground as an envelope of emissivity 0.85 (C8). Bare aluminium fins (emissivity about 0.1) would not; fixed by painting the fins and plate underside with a matt high-emissivity paint
law: Radiation from a grey envelope, h_r = 4 eps sigma T^3; painted metal about 0.9

claim: On a peak day (1000 W/m2, 40 C air) a dry bed stagnates near 133 C and the glazing inner skin near 106 C [D6], below the 130 C rating of the specified glazing (was checked as the bed at 785 W/m2; independent review)
law: Polycarbonate service rating applies to the sheet; inner skin from the film model of DWD-CAL-001 D2; DWD-DEC-001 decision of 2026-10-02

claim: Surfaces touched in normal use stay at or below 60 C: glazing outer skin 55 C, fins 47 C [D2, D3]
law: PR-013 touch limit of 60 C; contact burn thresholds depend on material and contact time (EN ISO 13732-1, values to confirm)

claim: After one 90 % RH night the salt solution fills 47 % of the gel's pores [E3], so no brine drains out
law: Solution volume (Conde activity, solution density) against 3.0 L of pore volume
check: 0.471179 of pore volume <= 1 of pore volume

claim: The fan's 65 % RH cut-out (restart below 60 %) sits below the 71 % RH at which the pores fill at equilibrium [E2]
law: Logger rule against the pore-filling humidity; lowered from 70 % RH, 1 point below pore filling and inside a low-cost sensor's tolerance, by Amish on 2026-10-25 (DWD-DEC-001 item 3)
closed_by: DWD-CAL-001 E3 to E5; DWD-DEC-001 item 3

claim: The 10 W panel covers the fan and logger: 23.6 Wh per day of load [F1]
law: Daily energy budget

claim: Two ground anchors each rated 250 N in uplift hold the unit in a 25 m/s gust; each must carry 234 N [H4] (96 N at the earlier 20 m/s [H5]). Was 100 N, a 6 % margin at 20 m/s (independent review)
law: Dynamic pressure, force coefficient 1.2 on 1.1 m2, overturning about the downwind legs with a factor of 1.5; anchor rating in the site soil to confirm when bought; design wind speed a 25 m/s gust until the site value is known (decided by Amish 2026-10-25, DWD-DEC-001 item 4)

claim: The 20 x 5 mm deck bars carry the trays, sorbent, water, absorbers and screens (about 52 N on the centre bar over 1,016 mm)
law: Simply supported bar, sigma = M / (I / c); 6063-T5 aluminium yield about 110 MPa with a factor of 2

claim: Brine-wetted parts survive hot CaCl2 solution: tray insides, floors, absorbers and drip screens in black PTFE-coated aluminium, the floor mesh PTFE-coated glass fibre. Was bare aluminium and a stainless woven mesh, which pit in chloride brine and, above about 60 C, risk chloride stress corrosion cracking
law: Chloride pitting of aluminium; chloride stress corrosion cracking of 304 and 316 is rare below 60 C (SSINA), the beds run to about 110 C; PTFE is inert to CaCl2 and rated to 260 C
check: Bare metal fails the 300-cycle life; coated parts within known science, coating damage carried in the design FMEA

claim: The composite keeps 80 % or more of its capacity over 300 cycles
law: CaCl2 does not decompose below about 175 C; ordinary silica gel can crack when wetted with solution, so a water-resistant grade is specified (DWD-DEC-001, to confirm item 1)

claim: The lumped bed model holds although heat enters at the plate on top: about 16 K drop through the 9.3 mm bed at noon; desorbing at the mid-depth temperature the yield is 0.41 L per day [C12]
law: Conduction through a packed bed, k about 0.2 W/(m K)
check: Yield falls from 0.44 to 0.41 L per day; PR-001 at risk under this sensitivity

claim: Condensate chloride stays below 250 mg/L: brine cannot reach the plate (pores never fill, sumps, no line of sight)
law: EU Directive 2020/2184 indicator value 250 mg/L; WHO taste threshold about 250 mg/L

claim: Collected water is free of harmful microbes once treated; the device itself is not a treatment step
law: Condensate is near distilled but picks up dust and microbes from surfaces and the bottle; boiling or disinfection before drinking
check: Documents require treatment before drinking; laboratory test needed (TRL 4)

claim: Pessimistic combination of the calculation's uncertainties (bed temperature drop and half the light through the absorber holes absorbed): 0.37 L per day [C13] against 0.44 on the lumped model
law: Independent review: the sensitivities were never combined
check: PR-001 not met on paper; range to be narrowed by measuring absorptance and isotherms (TRL 4)

claim: Parts near the hot interior stay inside their ratings on a peak day (bed about 133 C): plywood and PIR walls, EPDM seals, silicone, PTFE coatings
law: Gap air at about the mean of bed and air (about 85 C); fan, battery and electronics are outside the box; PTFE 260 C, silicone and EPDM typically above 130 C, PIR and plywood ratings to confirm with suppliers
check: Supplier ratings to confirm (DWD-DEC-001, to confirm item 12)

claim: The yield simulation conserves energy: unaccounted heat at dusk 0.08 kWh is sensible heat left in the bed
law: Sensible heat of the bed, trays and absorbers (about 7 kJ/K) over its rise at dusk

claim: Option B: a high-emissivity panel under a clear night sky runs about 10 K below the air
law: Net radiation to a sky of emissivity 0.75 (Berdahl and Martin) against convection at 5 W/(m2 K)

claim: Option B makes no water at the design point: the panel (10.1 C) stays above the dew point (6.0 C at 40 % RH; -0.6 C at 25 %)
law: Dew forms only on a surface below the dew point; field data show no condensation below about 71 % RH (Atashi et al., 2021)

claim: Option C: with the cloth at 80 C and the glazing at 50 C the brine dries to about 52 wt %, and takes up about 0.7 kg overnight at 40 % RH by natural convection
law: Regeneration ends where aw x psat(cloth) = psat(glazing): 52 wt %; night equilibrium 40.1 wt %; mass transfer 2.1 mm/s on 3.2 m2 of cloth (estimate)

claim: Option C's yield hinges on the cloth temperature: with the cloth at 70 C the brine dries only to about 44 wt % and takes up about 0.27 kg overnight
law: Same balance with psat(50 C) / psat(70 C): 44.0 wt % against 40.1 wt % at night

claim: Option C collects about 0.2 L per day (cloth at 70 C) to 0.5 L per day (cloth at 80 C) at the design point, far below the 2.5 L per m2 per day reported for unstated test conditions (Kabeel, 2007)
law: Solar still collection efficiency about 0.7 (estimate): 0.19 to 0.51 L per day
